model.name: Version / Change History
model.purpose: Attach revision identity, predecessor and successor lineage, compatibility and deprecation, change notes, and migration or patch paths to any versionable resource, independently of storage format.
model.scope_statement: This mixin describes how a resource is identified as a revision, how it sits in a version series versus a snapshot, how it relates to predecessors and replacements, how compatibility and lifecycle status are declared, and how change notes and operational deltas support migration. It aligns DCAT 3, PROV-O, OWL 2, DCMI, PAV, Semantic Versioning 2.0.0, DataCite versioning practice and IETF JSON Patch; it does not own the host resource, its content, its agents, or its access-control audit trail.
in_scope: Revision identifiers including version labels, version IRIs, canonical versus versioned identifiers, and pre-release or build metadata when a declared scheme uses them.
Version series versus immutable snapshots, including current-version pointers and has-version hierarchies.
Predecessor, successor, earlier-version and replacement or supersession relations, including qualified revision where needed.
Compatibility, incompatibility, deprecation and steward-defined major versus minor change class.
Lifecycle of a revision: draft or pre-release, freeze on release, generation and invalidation times, withdrawal.
Change notes between this version and the previous one, and operational migration artefacts such as sequential patches.
Integrity evidence for a frozen revision (checksum, concurrency precondition) and retention of prior versions at their version identifiers.
out_of_scope: Full provenance of who performed the change, with which activity, tools and sources; that belongs to a Provenance sibling using PROV agent, activity, attribution and qualified influence.
Host-entity identity assignment for the unversioned resource, party or dataset; version identity is additional to, not a substitute for, the master identifier of the host.
Dataset series membership and ordered collection links (first, last, previous-in-series), which DCAT distinguishes from previousVersion.
Format, encoding or distribution variants (dcterms:isFormatOf / hasFormat) that do not change content.
Translations, quotations, compilations and other derivations that are not revisions.
Source-control working trees, remotes, branches and merge-commit graphs as a complete SCM model.
Package dependency resolution, range syntax and lockfiles.
Access-control audit logs, security events and catalog-record modification history except where they must be distinguished from resource versioning.
Spatial location of authors or creators.
Content payload of the versioned resource.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Provenance (PROV-O agent, activity, attribution, qualified influence)
boundary_notes.distinction: wasRevisionOf and qualifiedRevision record that one entity is a revision of another; they do not record who revised it, with which activity, or from which sources. Agent, activity, generated-by and qualified attribution belong to Provenance. This mixin keeps the revision relation, times of generation or invalidation of the revision itself, and change notes.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Host identity / identifier of the unversioned resource
boundary_notes.distinction: OWL 2 separates an ontology IRI (the series) from a version IRI (one revision). DataCite separates a canonical DOI from version DOIs. A version label is not the host identifier, and a date is not an identifier.
DCAT dcat:prev, dcat:first and dcat:last order distinct resources in a series. dcat:previousVersion orders snapshots of the same resource. Mixing these relations is a classification error.
DCMI states that version changes imply substantive content change rather than differences in format. DCAT distributions and dcterms:hasFormat are not revisions.
DCAT CatalogRecord listing and modification dates describe the catalog entry, not the versioned resource. PROV may describe registration change; that is not a resource revision.
Append-only access and exception logs are not a version history. JSON Patch If-Match is a concurrency precondition on a change, not an audit event store.

bundles.name: Revision identity
bundles.description: How a revision is named and addressed, and how a versioned snapshot is distinguished from the abstract or mutable series it specialises.
bundles.rationale: Operators cannot create or resolve a revision without a version indicator, a version-specific identifier where one exists, and a clear split between the series and a frozen snapshot. OWL 2, DCAT, PAV, SemVer and DataCite all make this split, with different identifier kinds.

layers.name: Version indicators and identifier kinds
layers.description: Literal version names, scheme and grammar, pre-release and build metadata, and version-specific IRIs or DOIs versus the series identifier.

findings.name: Version label or indicator
findings.description: A version indicator is a name or identifier of a resource revision. DCAT dcat:version (equivalent to pav:version) is an rdfs:Literal and DCAT does not prescribe syntax, referring to DWBP Best Practice 7. Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 does prescribe X.Y.Z with optional pre-release and build metadata when that scheme is declared. DataCite Version is a string that may be incremented in place for minor changes. owl:versionInfo is a free-text version designation. A date is not a version identifier.

questions.text: What version indicator string is assigned to this revision, and under which versioning scheme is it interpreted?
If Semantic Versioning is declared, what are the major, minor, patch, pre-release and build-metadata components and the computed precedence key?
Which master system or steward assigned the version indicator, and is that assignment unique within the series?
Is the recorded indicator a true version name rather than a date, checksum, or host identifier used as a substitute?
If a pre-release label is present, is the revision declared unstable and not required to meet the compatibility of the associated normal version?

data_elements.name: Version indicator
data_elements.description: Literal version name or identifier of this revision (dcat:version / pav:version / DataCite Version / owl:versionInfo).

data_elements.name: Version scheme
data_elements.description: Declared interpretation of the indicator, for example semver-2.0.0, datacite-version, owl-versioninfo, free-text, or a Dimension-local scheme. Alignment, not automatic conformance.

data_elements.name: SemVer core triple
data_elements.description: Non-negative major, minor and patch integers without leading zeroes when SemVer is used.

data_elements.name: SemVer pre-release identifiers
data_elements.description: Dot-separated pre-release identifiers; a pre-release has lower precedence than the associated normal version.

data_elements.name: SemVer build metadata
data_elements.description: Build metadata ignored when determining precedence.

artifacts.name: Version indicator issuance record
artifacts.description: Master-system record of the assigned version label (registry version field, package tag, ontology versionInfo). Serial if the issuing system emits numbered releases.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the issuing registry's version record identifier if present; else a governed IRI of the issuance; else a Dimension UUID. Do not use the release date as the identifier.

findings.name: Version IRI versus series or canonical identifier
findings.description: OWL 2: an ontology MAY have an ontology IRI identifying the series and a version IRI identifying that version; a version IRI requires an ontology IRI; the pair identifies a member of an ontology series; exactly one version is current. The current document SHOULD be accessible at the ontology IRI and at the version IRI; prior versions SHOULD remain accessible only at their version IRIs. DataCite: a new major version SHOULD receive a new DOI; a canonical DOI MAY represent all versions, linked with HasVersion / IsVersionOf. DCAT/PAV treat the unversioned resource as distinct from versioned snapshots.

questions.text: What is the series, ontology, or canonical identifier of the unversioned resource this revision belongs to?
What version-specific IRI, DOI, or master-system identifier identifies this exact revision?
Should this revision be retrievable at the series identifier, only at the version identifier, or both because it is the current version?
Did this change mint a new persistent identifier, or reuse the previous identifier with an updated version label?
Is the combination of series identifier and version identifier unique, and are reserved-vocabulary IRIs avoided as version IRIs?

data_elements.name: Series or ontology IRI
data_elements.description: Identifier of the ontology series, mutable resource, or canonical work that this revision specialises.

data_elements.name: Version IRI or version DOI
data_elements.description: Identifier of this specific revision. Priority: authoritative master-system identifier; governed global IRI or DOI; Dimension UUID or ULID.

data_elements.name: Current at series IRI
data_elements.description: True if this revision's document SHOULD also be accessible via the series or ontology IRI.

data_elements.name: Canonical DOI
data_elements.description: Optional DOI representing all versions of the resource, distinct from version DOIs.

artifacts.name: Versioned document at version IRI
artifacts.description: The ontology document or resource representation that SHOULD be accessible via the version IRI (and via the series IRI if current).
artifacts.identity_strategy: The version IRI or version DOI is the artefact identity. If the master system uses another key, record that first. Do not identify the artefact by its issued date.

layers.name: Snapshot versus abstract or mutable resource
layers.description: A revision may be a frozen snapshot related to a mutable permalink or abstract resource.

findings.name: Snapshot specialisation of an abstract resource
findings.description: PAV and DCAT: an unversioned or abstract resource dcat:hasVersion / pav:hasVersion several versioned snapshots; dcat:hasCurrentVersion / pav:hasCurrentVersion points at the permalink snapshot of current content. PROV: each snapshot is a specializationOf the long-standing resource and alternateOf other snapshots; a new snapshot wasRevisionOf the previous. DCAT's hasVersion is narrower than dcterms:hasVersion, which also covers editions and adaptations.

questions.text: Is the host identifier a mutable permalink, an abstract series, or itself an immutable snapshot?
Which abstract or permalink resource does this snapshot specialise, and which other snapshots are its alternates?
Is the has-version link a DCAT/PAV lifecycle snapshot, or a broader DCMI edition or adaptation that should not be treated as a revision chain member?
Which snapshot is designated as the current equivalent content of the mutable resource?

data_elements.name: Mutability class
data_elements.description: Whether the described resource is mutable-permalink, abstract-series, or immutable-snapshot.

data_elements.name: Specialisation of abstract resource
data_elements.description: Reference to the general resource of which this snapshot is a more specific entity (prov:specializationOf).

data_elements.name: Alternate snapshots
data_elements.description: Other snapshots presenting aspects of the same thing (prov:alternateOf).

data_elements.name: Has-version snapshots
data_elements.description: Versioned resources of this abstract resource (dcat:hasVersion / pav:hasVersion).

artifacts.name: Snapshot resource
artifacts.description: Frozen content of the resource at this revision, distinct from the mutable permalink.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the snapshot's version IRI or master revision identifier; if none, a Dimension UUID. Dates are not identifiers.

bundles.name: Lineage, predecessor and replacement
bundles.description: How revisions form a chain or hierarchy, how one version supersedes another, and how the current member of a series is designated.
bundles.rationale: DCAT states that previousVersion and hasVersion are the properties necessary to specify a version chain and hierarchy. DataCite and DCMI add supersession pairs. OWL 2 and ADMS add current/last and next/prev navigation, with known conflicts of meaning.

layers.name: Predecessor, successor and supersession
layers.description: Direct previous version, earlier versions, next version, and replacement that displaces a prior resource.

findings.name: Previous-version and earlier-version chain
findings.description: dcat:previousVersion is equivalent to pav:previousVersion, a subproperty of prov:wasRevisionOf, and specifies a version chain of snapshots from revisions in a life-cycle. PAV treats previousVersion as the direct ancestor and hasEarlierVersion as any earlier version; previousVersion is normally functional. owl:priorVersion annotates a prior ontology version. ADMS adms:prev/next also mean previous/next version of an Asset, but DCAT 3 replaced that navigation with dcat:previousVersion and warns that dcat:prev is series order, not version order. Merge histories with multiple parents are not specified by PAV or DCAT and are a gap.

questions.text: What is the direct previous version of this revision, and is that link asserted as wasRevisionOf / previousVersion rather than a generic derivation?
Which earlier versions are known, either by walking the previousVersion chain or by explicit hasEarlierVersion links?
What next or successor version, if any, is recorded (adms:next, DataCite IsPreviousVersionOf inverse, or Dimension successor)?
Does this revision have more than one direct predecessor, as in a merge, even though PAV previousVersion is normally functional?
Has the operator confused dcat:prev (previous in a dataset series) with dcat:previousVersion (previous snapshot of the same resource)?

data_elements.name: Previous version
data_elements.description: Direct previous snapshot in the lineage (dcat:previousVersion / pav:previousVersion / owl:priorVersion / adms:prev as aligned, with conflict recorded).

data_elements.name: Was revision of
data_elements.description: PROV revision derivation; the derived entity contains substantial content from the original.

data_elements.name: Earlier versions
data_elements.description: Any earlier version, not only the direct ancestor (pav:hasEarlierVersion).

data_elements.name: Next version
data_elements.description: Successor version if recorded (adms:next).

data_elements.name: Qualified revision
data_elements.description: Optional prov:qualifiedRevision / prov:Revision influence node when extra attributes are needed.

artifacts.name: Version lineage map
artifacts.description: Directed map of previousVersion / wasRevisionOf / next links for the series, serialised independently of store.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by series IRI plus a Dimension UUID for this map instance; regenerate from links rather than treating dates as identity.

findings.name: Replacement and supersession
findings.description: dcterms:replaces / isReplacedBy record that one resource supplants, displaces or supersedes another and are used when only one version is valid. DataCite IsNewVersionOf / IsPreviousVersionOf link editions when one version supersedes another and both DOIs remain. DCAT points to section 11.1.2 for versions replaced by other ones. Replacement is not identical to previousVersion: a chain of historical snapshots may keep all versions citable while a replaces link marks which is valid.

questions.text: Which prior resource does this revision supplant, displace or supersede, and does the prior resource remain citable?
If persistent identifiers are used, is this identifier linked as IsNewVersionOf the previous edition and the previous as IsPreviousVersionOf this one?
Is only one version valid in this chain, as in successive drafts of a contract, or are historical snapshots still in force for citation?
Who authorised the replacement, and at what event time versus observation time?

data_elements.name: Replaces
data_elements.description: Resources this revision supplants (dcterms:replaces).

data_elements.name: Is replaced by
data_elements.description: Resources that supplant this revision (dcterms:isReplacedBy).

data_elements.name: Is new version of
data_elements.description: DataCite relation: this is a new edition of the referenced resource.

data_elements.name: Single valid version in chain
data_elements.description: True when the chain is a validity chain rather than a citable snapshot history.

artifacts.name: Replacement or supersession notice
artifacts.description: Statement that this revision displaces another, including remaining citation rights for the old identifier.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system notice identifier if issued; else governed IRI; else Dimension UUID.

layers.name: Version set and current member
layers.description: Listing all versions of an abstract resource and designating the current one.

findings.name: Current version pointer and version set
findings.description: dcat:hasCurrentVersion / pav:hasCurrentVersion relates an abstract resource to one snapshot usable as a permalink to current content. adms:last links to the current or latest Asset. OWL 2: creating a new current version SHOULD replace the document at the ontology IRI while leaving prior version IRIs in place. DataCite HasVersion lists specific versions from a canonical DOI. Exactly one current version per OWL ontology series is the convention; parallel current branches are a gap.

questions.text: What are all known versioned snapshots of this abstract or canonical resource?
Which snapshot is the current version, who designated it, and should the series IRI now resolve to it?
If a canonical identifier exists, is each specific version linked with HasVersion / IsVersionOf in both directions?
Are multiple snapshots simultaneously designated current (branches), which OWL series convention does not allow?
After a new current version is published, do prior versions remain resolvable at their version IRIs or DOIs?

data_elements.name: Current version
data_elements.description: The snapshot designated as current content (dcat:hasCurrentVersion / pav:hasCurrentVersion / adms:last).

data_elements.name: All versions
data_elements.description: All versioned snapshots of the abstract resource (dcat:hasVersion, DataCite HasVersion).

data_elements.name: Is version of
data_elements.description: The canonical or unversioned resource this snapshot instantiates (DataCite IsVersionOf, inverse of hasVersion).

artifacts.name: Current-version designation
artifacts.description: Record that a named snapshot is current for a series, including whether the series IRI was updated.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Series identifier plus designation event UUID; not the designation date alone.

bundles.name: Compatibility, change class and revision lifecycle
bundles.description: How a revision is classified as compatible or breaking, how deprecation and workflow status are declared, and how release freeze and generation or invalidation times are recorded.
bundles.rationale: OWL 2 annotates prior versions as backward compatible or incompatible. SemVer encodes the same idea in MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and forbids mutating a released version. DataCite leaves major versus minor to the steward. ADMS status and DCAT lifecycle guidance cover workflow, which is not the same as compatibility.

layers.name: Compatibility and change class
layers.description: Declarations of backward compatibility, incompatibility, and major/minor/patch or steward-defined change class.

findings.name: Backward compatibility and incompatibility
findings.description: owl:backwardCompatibleWith names a prior version compatible with the current one; owl:incompatibleWith names a prior version that is not. OWL 2 import closure SHOULD NOT include an ontology annotated incompatibleWith another in the closure, nor two versions from the same series. SemVer: increment MAJOR for incompatible public-API changes, MINOR for backward-compatible additions (and for deprecation), PATCH for backward-compatible bug fixes; 0.y.z is unstable. DataCite: individual stewards determine major versus minor; minor may reuse the DOI. These rules conflict and must be recorded as alignments, not claimed as one conformance.

questions.text: Which prior versions is this revision declared backward compatible with, and under which compatibility contract (public API, ontology identifiers, dataset schema)?
Which prior versions is this revision declared incompatible with, and what consumer action is required before upgrade?
What change class is assigned (SemVer major/minor/patch, DataCite major/minor, or local), and who defined that class?
If the SemVer major component is zero, is the public API explicitly treated as unstable so that anything MAY change?
If this resource is imported with others, does the import closure mix versions of the same series or include an incompatibleWith pair?

data_elements.name: Backward compatible with
data_elements.description: Prior versions with which this revision is compatible (owl:backwardCompatibleWith).

data_elements.name: Incompatible with
data_elements.description: Prior versions with which this revision is not backward compatible (owl:incompatibleWith).

data_elements.name: Change class
data_elements.description: major, minor, patch, or a steward-defined class. Not assumed to be SemVer unless version_scheme says so.

data_elements.name: Compatibility contract
data_elements.description: What must remain stable: public API, ontology IRIs and intended interpretations, or dataset schema.

artifacts.name: Compatibility declaration
artifacts.description: Record of backwardCompatibleWith / incompatibleWith / change class and the contract they refer to.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Version IRI of the declaring revision plus a Dimension UUID for the declaration.

findings.name: What counts as a version
findings.description: DCMI: version, edition or adaptation implies substantive content change, not format. DCAT: previousVersion is limited to life-cycle revisions; dcterms:hasVersion is broader. PROV: wasRevisionOf is a strict sub-relation of wasDerivedFrom; quotation and primary source are other derivations. DataCite treats translations as a different relationType pair. Dataset-series members are not versions.

questions.text: Is the related resource a life-cycle revision, a broader edition or adaptation, a format variant, a series member, a translation, or a non-revision derivation?
Did the content change substantively, or only the format, encoding, or distribution?
If PROV derivation holds, is wasRevisionOf applicable, or should wasQuotedFrom, hadPrimarySource, or generic wasDerivedFrom be used instead?

data_elements.name: Relation kind
data_elements.description: lifecycle-revision, dcterms-edition-or-adaptation, format-variant, series-member, translation, quotation, other-derivation.

data_elements.name: Substantive content change
data_elements.description: True when DCMI version semantics apply rather than format difference.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification of whether a relation is a revision is asserted as codes and flags on the mixin; no separate artefact is required unless the Dimension records a human decision notice under replacement-notice or version-notes.

layers.name: Status, freeze, generation and invalidation
layers.description: Workflow status, deprecation, immutability of released versions, and times bounding a revision.

findings.name: Workflow status and deprecation
findings.description: adms:status is the status of the resource in a particular workflow; DCAT does not prescribe a status vocabulary. owl:deprecated marks deprecated entities. SemVer: marking public API functionality deprecated MUST increment MINOR. Status (draft, released, deprecated, withdrawn) is not the same as compatibility class.

questions.text: What is the workflow status of this revision, from which concept scheme, and in which process?
Is this revision or any public contract it exposes marked deprecated, and did that trigger a minor version increment under SemVer?
Who is authorised to change status, and what evidence supports the current value?
Is a withdrawn or deprecated revision still backward compatible for consumers who already depend on it?

data_elements.name: Status concept
data_elements.description: SKOS concept for workflow status (adms:status). Scheme is Dimension-chosen; DCAT does not fix one.

data_elements.name: Deprecated
data_elements.description: Whether the revision or an exposed contract is deprecated (owl:deprecated).

data_elements.name: Deprecated elements
data_elements.description: Identifiers of deprecated public-API or ontology elements that forced a minor bump under SemVer.

artifacts.name: Deprecation or status notice
artifacts.description: Human-readable notice of deprecation, withdrawal, or status change.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system notice id or governed IRI; else Dimension UUID.

findings.name: Release freeze and revision times
findings.description: SemVer: once a versioned package has been released, its contents MUST NOT be modified; any modification MUST be a new version. Major 1.0.0 defines the public API. PROV: generatedAtTime and invalidatedAtTime bound the revision entity; wasInvalidatedBy names the ending activity. DCAT uses dcterms:issued as release date and dcterms:modified as update date of the resource, distinct from catalog-record dates. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately as RFC 3339 values.

questions.text: Has this revision been released, and is in-place mutation therefore forbidden?
At what event time was this revision generated, and at what time was that fact observed or ingested?
Has this revision been invalidated or withdrawn, at what time, and by which activity?
If dcterms:modified is set on a released revision, was that a forbidden in-place change or a metadata-only update that DataCite would treat as a minor version on the same identifier?
Are issued and modified times those of the resource revision, not the catalog record listing times?

data_elements.name: Released
data_elements.description: True when the revision has been issued as a frozen version.

data_elements.name: Generated at time
data_elements.description: Event time the revision entity came into existence (prov:generatedAtTime), RFC 3339 with seconds and offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Release date
data_elements.description: dcterms:issued for the resource revision.

data_elements.name: Modification date
data_elements.description: dcterms:modified; on a frozen SemVer release this should not reflect content mutation.

data_elements.name: Invalidated at time
data_elements.description: End of the revision entity's lifetime (prov:invalidatedAtTime).

data_elements.name: Observation or ingestion time
data_elements.description: When the Dimension recorded the event, distinct from event time.

artifacts.name: Frozen release manifest
artifacts.description: Manifest of the bits declared immutable at release, with identifier and generation time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Version IRI or registry version record id; checksum may corroborate but is not the identifier unless the master system is content-addressed.

bundles.name: Change notes, migration deltas and integrity evidence
bundles.description: Human-readable change history, operational patches that migrate one revision to another, and evidence that a frozen revision has not been altered.
bundles.rationale: ADMS versionNotes is the cross-vocabulary change description DCAT reuses. RFC 6902 supplies a sequential patch document suitable as a migration artefact. DCAT adds spdx:checksum on distributions; RFC 6902 uses If-Match as a concurrency test.

layers.name: Version notes and change log
layers.description: Textual description of changes between this version and the previous version.

findings.name: Version notes between this and the previous version
findings.description: adms:versionNotes is a description of changes between this version and the previous version of the Asset. DCAT says that in case of backward compatibility issues with the previous version, a textual description SHOULD be specified with this property. This is not a full provenance narrative and not a machine-applied patch.

questions.text: What is the description of changes between this version and the previous version, in which language?
If there are backward compatibility issues with the previous version, are they described in the version notes?
Who authored or approved the version notes, and is that distinct from the content author recorded in Provenance?
Do the notes cover added, removed, deprecated and incompatible contracts, or only a marketing summary?

data_elements.name: Version notes
data_elements.description: Literal description of changes versus the previous version (adms:versionNotes).

data_elements.name: Notes language
data_elements.description: Language tag of each versionNotes literal.

artifacts.name: Changelog
artifacts.description: Human-readable change history for this revision relative to its predecessor. May serialise adms:versionNotes plus structured sections.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Version IRI plus artefact UUID, or master-system changelog id.

layers.name: Patches, migration and integrity
layers.description: Machine-applied deltas from one revision to another, preconditions, and checksum or concurrency evidence.

findings.name: Sequential patch and migration path
findings.description: RFC 6902 defines a document that is an array of operations (add, remove, replace, move, copy, test) applied sequentially to a target until success or error. It is suitable for HTTP PATCH and for any structure that can be serialised as JSON. This mixin treats such a patch as a migration artefact between two revisions, not as the semantics of versioning. JSON, YAML and other encodings are projections. Media type application/json-patch+json identifies JSON Patch documents. Unrecognised members of an operation MUST be ignored.

questions.text: From which source revision to which target revision does this migration patch apply?
What ordered operations constitute the patch, and did a test operation fail?
Must consumers apply a migration (data rewrite, mapping, or recompile) before using this revision, given declared incompatibilities?
If the host is not JSON-shaped, what equivalent sequential delta form is used, and is JSON Patch only an alignment?
Who may apply the patch, and is application blocked when the target is a frozen released version?

data_elements.name: Patch source revision
data_elements.description: Revision the patch is applied to.

data_elements.name: Patch target revision
data_elements.description: Revision expected after successful application.

data_elements.name: Patch operations
data_elements.description: Ordered operation objects with op and path, and value or from as required by RFC 6902.

data_elements.name: Migration required
data_elements.description: Whether consumers must transform data or contracts to move from the previous version.

artifacts.name: JSON Patch document
artifacts.description: RFC 6902 patch document, media type application/json-patch+json, expressing the delta from one revision to another.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system patch id if issued; else hash of canonical patch bytes as a corroborating digest plus Dimension UUID as the governed id.

findings.name: Integrity, concurrency and retention of history
findings.description: DCAT 3 adds spdx:checksum on distributions as a digest. SemVer immutability makes a digest of a released revision evidence of non-mutation. RFC 6902 examples use If-Match as a precondition so a patch is not applied to the wrong base. OWL 2 requires prior versions to remain accessible at their version IRIs. Retention of superseded snapshots is therefore part of version history, not an afterthought.

questions.text: What checksum algorithm and digest identify the frozen bits of this revision or its distribution?
What concurrency token or If-Match value must be supplied before a patch or status change is accepted?
Has any comparison shown that a released revision's content changed after freeze?
How long must prior versions remain resolvable at their version identifiers, and when may a version be deleted or only tombstoned?
Do retained prior versions contain personal data that requires a different retention or redaction exception than the current version?

data_elements.name: Checksum algorithm
data_elements.description: Algorithm of the distribution or revision digest (as used with spdx:checksum).

data_elements.name: Checksum value
data_elements.description: Digest of the frozen revision or distribution.

data_elements.name: Concurrency token
data_elements.description: Precondition token analogous to If-Match for applying a patch to the intended base.

data_elements.name: History retention rule
data_elements.description: Policy for keeping prior version IRIs resolvable.

artifacts.name: Checksum or digest record
artifacts.description: Recorded digest of a frozen revision or its distribution.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Version IRI plus algorithm name; the digest value is evidence, not the primary identifier unless the master system is content-addressed.

functions.name: Assign version identity
functions.description: Mint or record a version indicator and, where used, a version IRI or version DOI distinct from the series or canonical identifier.
outputs: version IRI or master revision identifier
preconditions: Host is versionable in the adopting Dimension.
A date is not used as the identifier.
If OWL-style version IRIs are used, an ontology or series IRI already exists.
effects: A new revision identity exists and is unique within the series under the chosen scheme.
Alignment properties dcat:version / pav:version / owl:versionInfo / DataCite Version can be populated.

functions.name: Freeze released revision
functions.description: Mark a revision as released so its content MUST NOT be modified; further change requires a new version.
preconditions: Revision identity exists.
If SemVer is declared, public API is identified for 1.0.0 and later.
effects: In-place content mutation is forbidden.
Checksum evidence is bound to the revision.
Subsequent edits must create a successor revision.

functions.name: Link predecessor
functions.description: Assert previousVersion / wasRevisionOf / priorVersion from this revision to its direct ancestor, and optionally earlier versions.
preconditions: Both identities exist.
Relation kind is a life-cycle revision, not format or series membership.
If PAV functional previousVersion is enforced, at most one direct predecessor is stored in that slot.
effects: The version chain is extended.
Confusion with dcat:prev is rejected.

functions.name: Publish as current version
functions.description: Designate a snapshot as hasCurrentVersion / adms:last and, under OWL conventions, make it retrievable at the series IRI while leaving prior version IRIs in place.
preconditions: Snapshot is a version of the series.
Publisher is authorised.
effects: Exactly one current pointer is stored unless a documented branch exception applies.
Prior versions remain accessible at version identifiers.

functions.name: Declare compatibility
functions.description: Record backwardCompatibleWith, incompatibleWith, and change class relative to prior versions.
preconditions: A contract (API, ontology identifiers, or schema) is named.
SemVer rules are applied only if that scheme is declared.
effects: Consumers can test whether upgrade is safe.
DCAT SHOULD require versionNotes when compatibility issues exist.
OWL import-closure checks can use incompatibleWith.

functions.name: Supersede revision
functions.description: Assert dcterms:replaces / isReplacedBy and, where DOIs are used, IsNewVersionOf / IsPreviousVersionOf, optionally minting a new identifier for a major change.
outputs: optional new DOI or version IRI
preconditions: Steward has decided whether the change is major.
Identifier policy for reuse versus minting is known.
effects: Validity and citation rules for the old identifier are updated.
Both identifiers remain recorded.

functions.name: Deprecate revision or contract
functions.description: Set deprecated and workflow status, and under SemVer increment minor if public API is marked deprecated.
preconditions: Authority to change status is held by the version steward or delegated role.
effects: Consumers are warned.
Status is distinct from incompatibility.

functions.name: Apply migration patch
functions.description: Apply a sequential patch from a source revision toward a target, honouring test operations and concurrency preconditions.
inputs: JSON Patch or aligned delta document
preconditions: Source matches the concurrency token if present.
Target of each operation exists when RFC 6902 requires it.
Source is not a frozen released version unless the output is a new revision.
effects: Operations are applied in order until success or error.
A successful content-changing apply on a frozen version is recorded as a new revision, not an in-place edit.

functions.name: Compare version precedence
functions.description: Order two version indicators under SemVer precedence, or under a declared alternative scheme.
preconditions: Both indicators use the same declared scheme, or an explicit mapping exists.
effects: Build metadata is ignored under SemVer.
Pre-release is lower than the associated normal version.

functions.name: Record version notes
functions.description: Attach adms:versionNotes describing changes versus the previous version.
preconditions: Previous version is known, or notes state that this is the first version.
effects: Human-readable history is stored.
Compatibility issues SHOULD be described when present.

functions.name: Invalidate revision
functions.description: Bound the end of a revision's lifetime with invalidatedAtTime and optional invalidating activity, without deleting the history.
preconditions: Revision exists.
Deletion policy allows tombstone rather than silent erase of released history.
effects: Revision is no longer usable as current.
Identifier remains resolvable per retention rule.

composition.target: Host versionable resource in the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Carry revision identity, lineage, compatibility, lifecycle, notes and migration fields on any versionable entity without owning the entity type.

composition.target: Provenance (PROV agent, activity, attribution, qualified influence)
composition.purpose: Record who revised, with which activity and sources; this mixin only stores wasRevisionOf, times, and notes.
Keep series or canonical identifiers distinct from version IRIs, version DOIs and version labels.
Share RFC 3339 event versus observation timestamps; this mixin only uses them on generation, issue, modification and invalidation of revisions.
Keep dcat:prev/first/last out of version chains; series members are not snapshots of one resource.
Prevent treating format variants as versions; DCMI version means substantive content change.
Align dcat:version, previousVersion, hasVersion, hasCurrentVersion and related DCTERMS/ADMS properties without claiming DCAT catalog conformance.
Align wasRevisionOf, specializationOf, alternateOf, generatedAtTime, invalidatedAtTime and qualifiedRevision.
Align ontology IRI versus version IRI, current-version publication, priorVersion and compatibility annotations.

composition.target: DCMI Metadata Terms version and replacement properties
composition.purpose: Align hasVersion, isVersionOf, replaces, isReplacedBy and the content-versus-format rule.
Optional scheme for version indicators, precedence, freeze-on-release and bump rules.
Align pav:version, previousVersion, hasEarlierVersion, hasVersion, hasCurrentVersion; DCAT equivalentProperty links.
Align Version, IsNewVersionOf, IsPreviousVersionOf, HasVersion, IsVersionOf and canonical DOI practice.

composition.target: ADMS status, version notes and last/next/prev
composition.purpose: Align versionNotes and status; record that DCAT 3 superseded ADMS version-navigation properties.
Provide a sequential delta artefact for migration; encoding-specific, not the core semantics of revision identity.

owner_package_requirements: Designate a version steward authorised to assign version identifiers, freeze releases, set current version, and change status.
Declare the version scheme or schemes in force (SemVer 2.0.0, DataCite steward major/minor, OWL version IRI, free-text, or local) and record that they are alignments, not a single conformance claim.
Provide a namespace for version IRIs or bind to an external master system (package registry, DOI agency, ontology IRI policy).
State whether previousVersion is constrained to a single functional predecessor or whether multiple merge parents are stored as a documented extension.
Publish AGENTS.md with Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before agents operate on instances.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Prefer the master system's version IRI or DOI namespace. For Dimension-minted identifiers use a governed IRI under the Dimension namespace such as the series IRI plus a version segment, or a UUID/ULID when no dereferenceable version IRI exists. Do not put version identity in file extensions, commit dates, or storage collection names. Keep the series IRI stable; mint a new version IRI per frozen revision, following OWL 2 accessibility conventions when IRIs are used.

canonicalization_rules: A revision identity is the master-system identifier if present; else the version IRI or DOI; else a Dimension UUID or ULID. Version labels are not unique keys by themselves.
Normalize SemVer indicators by parsing the 2.0.0 grammar; drop build metadata from precedence keys; reject leading zeroes in numeric components.
Treat previousVersion, wasRevisionOf and owl:priorVersion as the same lineage slot when mapping, but persist the originally asserted property.
Treat dcat:prev as out of this mixin.
Timestamps are RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z; store event time and observation time as separate fields.
Checksum comparisons use the declared algorithm on the frozen bytes, not on a later encoding.
patch_rules: Patches to mixin metadata of an unreleased revision may update notes, status and current-pointer; they must not rewrite a frozen content digest.
Content-changing RFC 6902 documents create or populate a successor revision; they are not in-place edits of a released version.
Patch operations apply in array order; on error, the apply fails and no partial success is published as a new frozen version.
Unrecognised operation members are ignored per RFC 6902.
If-Match or equivalent concurrency token is required when the source revision could have moved.
compatibility_rules: Do not claim SemVer, DCAT, OWL or DataCite conformance unless evidence of the declared scheme is stored.
A SemVer MAJOR increment or owl:incompatibleWith both mean unsafe upgrade; a DataCite 'major' is steward-defined and may only mean a new DOI.
Deprecation under SemVer requires a MINOR increment; owl:deprecated does not by itself change the version number.
Import or composition of two versions from the same series, or of a pair linked by incompatibleWith, is a validation failure unless an exception is recorded.
dcterms:hasVersion is broader than dcat:hasVersion; mappings must not silently narrow editions and adaptations into life-cycle snapshot chains.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier (registry version record, version DOI, ontology version IRI, package version as issued by the registry).
Governed global identifier or IRI assigned under the Dimension namespace policy.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. A date is not an identifier; a checksum is evidence unless the master system is content-addressed.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event time and observation or ingestion time separately as RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts (issuance records, frozen manifests, changelogs, patch documents, notices) use the version indicator plus a monotonic serial or the version IRI; never a bare date. Non-serial artefacts (lineage maps, checksum records) are identified by series plus artefact UUID.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Frozen releases carry a checksum of the declared bytes. Mixin metadata patches require a concurrency token. Digest mismatch on a released revision is an integrity incident, not a silent modify.

policies: Released revisions are immutable; corrections are new revisions with predecessor links.
Every non-initial revision SHOULD have a previousVersion or an explicit first-version flag.
Backward-compatibility issues SHOULD be described in adms:versionNotes.
Prior versions remain resolvable at version identifiers until the retention rule allows tombstone; silent deletion of released history is forbidden.
Format variants, translations and series members are not recorded as versions.
Version history is readable under the host's access policy; unreleased revisions and embargoed snapshots are restricted by default.

read: Resolve current version from a series identifier.
Return version indicator, compatibility declarations, notes, checksum and patch artefacts.
Compare precedence of two indicators under the declared scheme.
create: Assign revision identity and optional version IRI or DOI.
Create a snapshot, link predecessor, and optionally freeze.
Add changelog, checksum, and migration patch artefacts.
Mint related-identifier pairs when a new persistent identifier is issued.
update: Update version notes, status and deprecation on unreleased revisions.
Add successor or replaces links that do not mutate frozen content.
Correct observation-time metadata without changing event time.
delete: Do not erase a frozen released revision; invalidate and tombstone instead.
Unreleased drafts may be deleted if no identifier was publicly issued.
Honour legal hold and personal-data redaction exceptions without breaking the predecessor chain (replace payload with a redacted snapshot as a new revision if required).

roles.name: Version steward
responsibilities: Assign version identifiers under the declared scheme.
Freeze releases and designate current version.

roles.name: Compatibility reviewer
responsibilities: Classify change as compatible, incompatible, or steward major/minor.
Require version notes for breaking changes.
Advise SemVer bump when that scheme is declared.

roles.name: Publisher
responsibilities: Make the current snapshot retrievable at the series identifier.

roles.name: Migration author
responsibilities: Write sequential patches or migration instructions.
Attach test operations and concurrency preconditions.
Record non-JSON delta forms as alignments.

roles.name: History auditor
responsibilities: Review retention, tombstones and access exceptions.

roles.name: Consumer resolver
responsibilities: Apply migration before upgrade when required.

access.default_rule: Released, non-embargoed revisions and their lineage, notes and checksums inherit the host resource read policy. Unreleased drafts, embargoed snapshots and apply-patch are denied except to version steward, publisher, migration author and auditor roles. History is append-only for released revisions.
exceptions: Embargoed unpublished versions remain hidden until issue time.
Yanked or invalidated versions stay in lineage but MUST NOT be designated current.
Personal-data redaction may replace a snapshot payload via a new revision rather than editing history.
If-Match failure is a denied write, not a delete.
audit_requirements: Record who assigned, froze, designated current, deprecated, superseded, patched or invalidated a revision, with event time and observation time.
Record digest mismatches as integrity incidents.
Do not treat this audit as a substitute for a security event log.

read_order: AGENTS.md in the Dimension package root, to obtain Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL.
Specification URL for this mixin's canonical field and alignment rules.
Storage type URL for how revision graphs, artefacts and checksums are persisted.
Interface URL for resolve-current, walk-predecessor, freeze, patch-apply and compare-precedence.
Processes URL for freeze, supersede, deprecate, invalidate and retention workflows.

coverage.claim: This mixin covers revision identity, series versus snapshot, predecessor and replacement, compatibility and deprecation, freeze and invalidation times, version notes, sequential migration patches, and history retention, as aligned to DCAT 3, PROV-O, OWL 2, DCMI, PAV, SemVer 2.0.0, DataCite versioning guidance and RFC 6902. It does not provide a single unified versioning theory and does not cover SCM graphs, CalVer, or package-manager yank semantics.

checklist.notes: Version indicator, version IRI/DOI versus series/canonical identifier, SemVer components, and identity priority are modelled.
Workflow status, deprecation, freeze-on-release, pre-release instability, and invalidation are modelled.
previousVersion, wasRevisionOf, hasVersion, hasCurrentVersion, replaces, DataCite version relation pairs, specializationOf and alternateOf are modelled.
generatedAtTime, issued, modified, invalidatedAtTime, and separate observation time as RFC 3339.
Revision relation and notes authorship are in scope; full agent/activity provenance is explicitly a sibling reference.
Version steward, assigning system, and status authority are modelled.
Scheme grammar, uniqueness, series versus version confusion, import-closure conflicts, and freeze violations are modelled.
Default read of released history, restriction of drafts, patch apply rights, and If-Match preconditions.
Prior versions remain at version IRIs; tombstone versus erase; legal hold and redaction via new revision.
Alignments to DCAT, PROV, OWL, DCMI, PAV, SemVer, DataCite, ADMS and RFC 6902 with conflicts recorded.
owl:backwardCompatibleWith / incompatibleWith and SemVer bump rules, with DataCite steward major/minor conflict flagged.
RFC 6902 sequential patch artefact and migration-required flag.
SemVer released-version freeze plus checksum evidence.
Direct previous, earlier versions, next, and an explicit gap for merge DAGs.
Life-cycle revision versus format, series member, translation and other derivation.
Location of creation is Provenance/authoring, not revision identity.

known_omissions: Git-style merge and octopus-merge predecessor DAGs; PAV previousVersion is normally functional and DCAT describes a chain, not a DAG.
Calendar Versioning (CalVer) and other non-SemVer, non-OWL identifier grammars.
Package-manager yank/unpublish/retract semantics (npm, crates.io) as distinct from PROV invalidation.
FHIR meta.versionId / If-Match resource versioning, MediaWiki revision ids, and Software Heritage SWHID as primary identifiers.
Schema-evolution compatibility (Avro, Protocol Buffers) as a specialised contract.
Content-addressed identity (git SHA, IPFS CID) as the master identifier; checksums are evidence here.
Parallel current branches as first-class OWL-incompatible series.
Legal corrigendum versus new edition in legislation and ISO document control.
Automated semantic-release and changelog-generation tool contracts.
Embargo clocks beyond a simple unreleased/released flag.
conflicts: ADMS last/next/prev versus DCAT previousVersion/hasCurrentVersion: ADMS 2.00 notes that DCAT replaced ADMS version-navigation properties; both remain as alignments.
dcat:prev (series order) versus dcat:previousVersion (snapshot lineage) share informal wording but are disjoint in DCAT.
dcterms:hasVersion includes editions and adaptations; dcat:hasVersion / pav:hasVersion are limited to life-cycle snapshots.
SemVer forbids modifying a released version; DataCite allows the same DOI with an updated Version for steward-defined minor changes.
DataCite major versus minor is steward-defined; SemVer major is an incompatible public-API change.
PAV previousVersion is normally one direct ancestor; merge revisions need multiple parents.
OWL 2 expects exactly one current version per series IRI; product branches may need several currents.
owl:backwardCompatibleWith is identifier-interpretation compatibility for ontologies, not SemVer public-API compatibility.
regional_assumptions: Status concepts are not fixed; EU ADMS-SKOS or a local SKOS scheme may be used.
DataCite DOI practice is centred on research outputs; it is an alignment for other domains, not a requirement.
SemVer is software-API-centred and is optional for datasets and documents.
RFC 3339 timestamps with explicit offset or Z are required in this Dimension regardless of local date formats.
JSON Patch is the normative sequential-delta alignment; non-JSON hosts must record an equivalent form.
adversarial_checks: Reject treating a format or encoding change as a new version (DCMI content-versus-format rule).
Reject storing dataset-series dcat:prev in the previousVersion slot.
Reject mutating bytes of a SemVer-released revision and only bumping dcterms:modified.
Reject using a date, catalog-record id, or filename as the revision identifier.
Reject claiming SemVer conformance when no public API is declared.
Reject collapsing dcterms:hasVersion adaptations into a DCAT snapshot chain.
Reject dropping prior version IRIs when publishing a new current version.
Reject applying RFC 6902 without If-Match to a moving mutable permalink and calling the result the same frozen version.
Reject modelling translations (DataCite IsTranslationOf) as IsNewVersionOf.
Reject a single functional predecessor when the evidence is a merge, without flagging the DAG gap.
